proposals.before: Gao Wanxing of Yan broke from Chongben and came over to Liang. Zhu Wen sent Zhijun to join him; they took Dan, Yan, Bin, and Fang. Zhijun was made acting Grand Mentor and Palace Attendant and enfeoffed Prince of Dapeng.
proposals.after: Gao Wanxing of Yan broke from Chongben and came over to Liang. Zhu Wen sent Zhijun to join him; they took Dan, Yan, Fu, and Fang. Zhijun was made acting Grand Mentor and Palace Attendant and enfeoffed Prince of Dapeng.
proposals.reason: Chinese 鄜州 is Fu, not Bin (邠); the idiomatic list wrongly uses Bin for 鄜.

proposals.before: Once Bin and Fang were his, the Founder ordered Zhijun back against Bin. Zhijun would not march: the army had no grain.
proposals.after: Once Fu and Fang were his, the Founder ordered Zhijun back against Bin. Zhijun would not march: the army had no grain.
proposals.reason: Chinese 已下鄜、坊 refers to Fu and Fang already taken, not Bin; Bin (邠州) is only the next target.

proposals.before: Li Keyong brought him to Taiyuan, gave him a grand house, and set him above the other generals.
proposals.after: The Prince of Jin brought him to Taiyuan, gave him a grand house, and set him above the other generals.
proposals.reason: Chinese has 晉王, not Li Keyong; by this campaign the Prince of Jin was Li Cunxu (later Zhuangzong).

proposals.before: Li Keyong made him acting Grand Mentor and Secretariat co-equal, military governor of Tianping and southeastern-route pacifier, set above the other generals.
proposals.after: The Prince of Jin made him acting Grand Mentor and Secretariat co-equal, military governor of Tianping and southeastern-route pacifier, set above the other generals.
proposals.reason: Chinese has 晉王; after 908 this is Li Cunxu, not Li Keyong.

proposals.before: Zhenming 1: Yang Shihou of Wei died. The Last Emperor, finding Wei troops proud and unruly, carved out Xiang, Cao, and Wei for a new Zhaode command under Zhang Jun;
proposals.after: Zhenming 1: Yang Shihou of Wei died. The Last Emperor, finding Wei troops proud and unruly, carved out Xiang, Chan, and Wei for a new Zhaode command under Zhang Yun;
proposals.reason: 澶 is Chan (not Cao), and 張筠 is Zhang Yun (not Zhang Jun), matching the earlier Suzhou prefect.

proposals.before: As a youth he was a tooth officer at Huazhou.
proposals.after: As a youth he was a tooth officer at Hua Prefecture (滑州).
proposals.reason: 滑州 is Hua (滑), easily confused with 華州; clarify the prefecture intended by the Chinese.

decisions.reason: Focus unit lists 丹、延、鄜、坊; 鄜 is Fuzhou (Fu), distinct from 邠 (Bin) in s0009 and s0012. The idiomatic wrongly renders 鄜 as Bin; Fu restores the toponym.
太祖已下鄜、坊 names Fu and Fang as already taken; 邠州 appears only as the next target in 復攻邠州. Replacing the first Bin with Fu corrects the place already held without changing the Bin campaign order.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 太祖已下鄜、坊，遣知俊復攻邠州

decisions.reason: Chinese has 晉王, not a personal name. The prior idiomatic invents Li Keyong; after Hui’s surrender in s0049 and before 莊宗立 in s0051, 晉王 is Li Cunxu. “The Prince of Jin” matches the source wording.
Focus unit opens 晉王拜寶; the idiomatic wrongly names Li Keyong. Adjacent s0080’s 莊宗 shows this is Li Cunxu’s Jin court. “The Prince of Jin” restores the title actually written.
Chinese 分相、澶、衞 has 澶 (Chan), not 曹 (Cao), and 以張筠為節度使: 筠 is Yun, not Jun. Both proposed corrections match the characters; the rest of the sentence can stand.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 乃分相、澶、衞三州建昭德軍，以張筠為節度使

decisions.reason: 滑州 is already rendered accurately as Huazhou; adding “Hua Prefecture (滑州)” is only disambiguation style, not a meaning error. Preserve the existing idiomatic wording.
